::: {.tut-standfirst}
The first step inside the application is loading your occurrence spreadsheet. Saíra accepts CSV and Excel and takes care of encoding and separator detection for you.
:::

## Accepted formats

| Format | Extension | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Delimited text | `.csv`, `.tsv`, `.txt` | Comma, semicolon or tab — detected automatically |
| Excel | `.xlsx`, `.xls` | You choose which sheet (tab) to import |

Each **row** must be one occurrence (a record of an organism in a place and moment) and each **column** an attribute — catalog number, species, date, locality, collector, and so on.

## Loading the file

To practice this and the next steps, download the sample spreadsheet [`ocorrencias-exemplo.csv`](../../assets/exemplo/ocorrencias-exemplo.csv) — a small, deliberately imperfect dataset.

On the **Upload** tab, drag the file onto the indicated area or click to select it.

1. **Select the file.** Drop the CSV/Excel onto the upload area.
2. **Check the reading.** Saíra shows a preview of the first rows — verify that the columns are split correctly.
3. **Adjust if needed.** If the encoding or separator was read incorrectly (broken accents, everything in a single column), change the option and the preview updates.

```{=html}
<figure class="shot">
  <div class="frame"><span class="ph-label">screenshot · upload area and preview</span></div>
  <figcaption><b>Figure 1.</b> Upload area with the preview of the first rows and the encoding and separator controls.</figcaption>
</figure>
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## Accents showing up wrong?
This is almost always an encoding issue. Brazilian spreadsheets are usually in **UTF-8** or **Latin-1 (ISO-8859-1)**. If "São Paulo" became "S&atilde;o Paulo", change the encoding on import until the preview looks right.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## The whole spreadsheet opened in a single column?
That's the wrong separator. Brazilian files often use a **semicolon (`;`)** because the comma is already the decimal separator. If the preview shows everything crammed into one column, switch the separator (`;`, `,` or tab) until the columns split correctly.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## Header on the first row
Saíra assumes that the **first row** contains the column names. Remove title rows, logos or merged cells before exporting from Excel — they get in the way of reading.
:::

## Camera-trap data

If your data come from camera traps, Saíra recognizes common structures of that kind of survey and helps organize them before mapping.

## Next steps

With the data loaded and displayed correctly, move on to **[Mapping fields to Darwin Core](03-dwc-mapping.qmd)**.
